What it does

Any job where another company has to act. For example:

  • Chase an overdue invoice, or dispute a charge from a distributor.
  • File a damage claim with a carrier, or request a certificate of insurance from a supplier.
  • Get a contract countersigned, or answer an auditor’s document request.

If it involves sending something out and getting an answer back, Mozart can run it.

Finance

  • Collect what customers owe you
  • Dispute charges you didn’t agree to
  • Answer vendor and auditor requests

Operations

  • Claim for short, late or damaged deliveries
  • Confirm orders and delivery dates with suppliers
  • Keep supplier documents current

Legal

  • Send agreements and get them signed
  • Collect certificates, licences and renewals
  • Respond to notices and information requests

These are examples. You describe the job and Mozart executes it.

How it works

Every job runs the same way.

Step 01

Find

Mozart picks the job up from your inbox, a portal or your ledger.

Step 02

Prepare

It pulls the invoice, the contract, the proof. Every number links back to the page it came from.

Step 03

Act

You approve. Mozart sends it by email, in the portal or as a file.

Step 04

Follow up

If they don’t answer, Mozart chases. You see every reply.

Step 05

Record

What happened, and how that company behaved, is kept for next time.

Nothing to migrate.
Nothing sent without you.

Works in your systems

Mozart reads your ledger, ERP and inbox and writes back only what you approve. Your team keeps working where it already does.

You approve before anything is sent

Remembers every company you deal with

Who to email, what format they want, how long they take. The next job starts ahead.

Before anything changes

Tested on your own work before it goes live.

Every job Mozart has run for you, and every call your team made on it, becomes a private test set. Nothing public, nothing borrowed from another company.

A change to a procedure, a model or the way Mozart acts is run against that set first, including the cases where the right answer is to stop and ask you. Only a version that passes goes live.
